See also: Appendix:Variations of "com"

Translingual

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Clipping of English Comanche or Spanish comanche.

Symbol

[edit]

com

  1. (international standards) ISO 639-3 language code for Comanche.

See also

[edit]
  • Wiktionary’s coverage of Comanche terms

English

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • com., COM

Pronunciation

[edit]
This entry needs pronunciation information. If you are familiar with the IPA or enPR then please add some!

Noun

[edit]

com (plural coms)

  1. Abbreviation of committee.
    Synonyms: cmte, comm
  2. Abbreviation of community.
  3. Abbreviation of communication.
    Synonym: comm
  4. Abbreviation of command.
    Synonym: cmd
  5. Abbreviation of comedy.
  6. Abbreviation of company.
  7. A player in a video game which is controlled by the computer rather than a human.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • com sec
  • intercom
  • quad com
  • rom com
  • rom-zom-com
  • sim-com
  • telecom
  • zom-com

Adjective

[edit]

com

  1. (Internet) Abbreviation of commercial; as in .com (the most known Internet top-level domain).
  2. Abbreviation of common.
    l. com. car. a. ― left common carotid artery

Derived terms

[edit]
  • dot-com

See also

[edit]
  • com ruou

Anagrams

[edit]
  • CMO, MCO, MOC, OMC, moc

Acehnese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Chamic *cum. Compare Malay cium, Bahnar chŭm.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈcɔm/

Verb

[edit]

com

  1. to kiss
  2. (transitive) to smell

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *quomō, from classical Latin quōmodō. Cognate with Spanish and Portuguese como. See also French comme and Italian come.

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • còm (obsolete)

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈkɔm]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈkom]
  • Audio:(file)

Adverb

[edit]

com

  1. (interrogative) how
  2. like
  3. (in comparisons, tan ... com) as ... as
Derived terms
[edit]
  • com a
  • com a màxim
  • com a mínim
  • com a molt
  • com ara
  • com està
  • com estàs
  • com et dius
  • com l'anell al dit
  • com que
  • com una exhalació
  • com va
  • tal com

Etymology 2

[edit]

Borrowed from Gaulish *kumbos (“curved”). Related to *kumbā (“valley”).

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • cóm (pre-2016)

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic, Valencia) [ˈkom]

Noun

[edit]

com m (plural coms)

  1. trough, manger
    Synonym: obi
  2. (geography) a steep-sided glacial valley with a level floor
    Synonym: vall d'obi
Related terms
[edit]
  • coma

Further reading

[edit]
  • “com” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.
  • “cóm” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.
  • “com”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “com”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007

    Old Occitan

    [edit]

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • con
    • cum

    Etymology

    [edit]

    From Vulgar Latin *quomo, from classical Latin quomōdo. Gallo-Romance cognate with Old French con, cum, etc.

    Conjunction

    [edit]

    com

    1. like; as

    Adverb

    [edit]

    com

    1. how (in what fashion)
      • 12th century, Bernard de Ventadour, E mainh genh se volv e's vira
        No sai com me contenha
        I don't know how to act

    References

    [edit]
    • Walther von Wartburg (1928–2002), “quomodo”, in Französisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch, volume 2: C Q K, page 1542

    Portuguese

    [edit]

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • c, c/ (abbreviation)
    • cum (eye dialect)
    • cõ (obsolete, abbreviation)

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese con, from Latin cum (“with”). Compare Fala and Galician con and Spanish con.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kõ/, /kũ/
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kõ/

    • Audio (Brazil):(file)
    • Audio (Brazil (São Paulo)):(file)
    • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
    • Rhymes: -õ
    • Hyphenation: com

    Preposition

    [edit]

    com

    2. with; against
      Synonym: contra
      Antonym: a favor de
      Lutamos com os nossos inimigos.
      We fight [against] our enemies.
      • 2005, J. K. Rowling, translated by Lia Wyler, Harry Potter e o Enigma do Príncipe [Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince] (Harry Potter; 6), Rio de Janeiro: Rocco, →ISBN, page 282:
        Tenho coisas mais importantes a discutir com você hoje à noite.
        I have more important things to discuss with you tonight.
    4. with; alongside; together with (in the company of)
      Synonyms: junto de, junto com, ao lado de
      Lutamos com os nossos amigos.
      We fight alongside our friends.
    6. with (as a part or accessory of)
      Antonym: sem
      Compramos uma casa com uma garagem e com dois andares.
      We bought a house with a garage and with two storeys.
    8. with (in support of)
      Synonym: a favor de
      Antonym: contra
      Quero saber se meus amigos estão comigo.
      I want to know whether my friends are with me.
    10. with; using (by means of)
      Synonyms: a, usando
      Antonym: sem
      Escrevi o artigo com um lápis.
      I wrote the article with a pencil.
    12. with (as a consequence of)
      Synonyms: por causa de, devido a
      Com a falência da fábrica, ficamos desempregados.
      With the bankruptcy of the factory, we ended up unemployed.
    14. with; having
      Synonym: tendo
      Antonym: sem
      Estou com a pior dor de cabeça que o mundo já viu.
      I have the worst headache the world has ever seen.

    Usage notes

    [edit]

    The following com + prepositional pronoun phrases have mandatory contractions:

    • com + mim → comigo
    • com + ti → contigo
    • com + si → consigo

    The following are mandatory except when the phrase is qualified by an adjective phrase, such as mesmos or todos:

    • com + nós → connosco (Portugal), conosco (Brazil)
    • com + vós → convosco

    Com + article contraction are colloquial, but are common in speech:

    • com + o → co
    • com + os → cos
    • com + a → ca
    • com + as → cas
    • com + um → cum
    • com + uns → cuns
    • com + uma → cuma
    • com + umas → cumas

    Quotations

    [edit]

    For quotations using this term, see Citations:com.

    [edit]

    Noun

    [edit]

    com m (genitive singular cuim, plural cuim)

    1. bosom, breast, chest
    2. trunk (body)
    3. stomach

    Derived terms
